title: Compact error does not mean a small error
promptMarkdown: Let $K$ be compact on an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$. Prove that $I+K$ is Fredholm of index zero without assuming $\|K\|<1$. Explain how the path $I+tK$ is used and give an example where $I+K$ is not invertible although its index is zero.
hintLadder: Use the two-sided compact-parametrix criterion first.
A locally constant integer on an interval is constant.
Subtract a rank-one projection from the identity.
